summary.headline: Muthoot Capital Q2 FY27 PAT of Rs 4.11 crore, AUM Rs 3,530 crore (+25% YoY), GNPA up to 4.61% with forward flow down to 0.50%.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as a consolidation period, highlighted the Brickwork upgrade to AA, and reported AUM of Rs 3,530 crore, up 25% YoY, with Q2 fresh disbursements of Rs 677 crore. Co-lending was run down to Rs 382 crore from Rs 791 crore a year earlier, lifting the blended yield, while borrowing costs fell by 0.61% for bank loans. Asset quality was mixed: GNPA rose to 4.61% from 5.76% a year ago (and was higher QoQ), but forward flow to NPA fell to 0.50% and impairment was Rs 21.44 crore in the quarter. Management reiterated a ~4% ROA goal, with CV and used car still in investment phase.

segments.name: Two-wheeler (core)
segments.commentary: Standalone book of Rs 2,656 crore with GNPA of about Rs 135 crore; management calls it the warhorse, with dealer channel at Rs 2,453 crore of AUM and 4.56% GNPA.

segments.name: Used car
segments.commentary: Book of about Rs 215 crore with GNPA of about Rs 4 crore (1.31%); still loss-making and in investment phase, with breakeven targeted for Q1 FY28.

segments.name: Commercial vehicle and construction equipment
segments.commentary: Combined book of about Rs 350-356 crore with GNPA near 0.35%; disbursements rose over 100% in H1, with breakeven targeted by end of FY27.

segments.name: Group relationship channel
segments.commentary: Rs 422 crore of AUM with 5.70% GNPA, a key driver of the elevated asset quality ratio.

segments.name: Co-lending
segments.commentary: Book fell 52% YoY to Rs 382 crore from Rs 791 crore; the last active partner was closed in Q1 and no new co-lending is being done.

segments.name: Fixed deposits
segments.commentary: Deposit book up about 250% YoY to Rs 155 crore; average ticket below Rs 5 lakh, with fresh collection above Rs 350 crore in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: AUM exit FY27 closer to Rs 4,200 crore.
Bank borrowing cost to fall a further 0.25-0.30% after the AA rating, and about 0.10% more by March 2027.
Disbursements expected at Rs 400+ crore per month in November onward, after Rs 306 crore in October (highest ever October).
Impairment expected to be contained at about 2% of the book by March 2027 results, per the CFO's comment.
Long-term goal of ~4% ROA maintained; CV breakeven targeted by end of FY27 and car breakeven by Q1 FY28.
Car and CV to rise to 50-60% of the book over the next two years.
capex_capacity: Commercial vehicle and used car underwriting scorecards and BREs to be moved in-house by December 2026, following the two-wheeler move.
Pan-India fixed deposit campaign launched after the AA rating allowed deposit-taking outside Kerala via the digital platform.
Liquidity: structural liquidity and ALM statements filed with RBI showing no cumulative mismatch in any bucket.
demand_pricing: Approval rates rose to about 70-75% from 45-50% after the in-house origination scorecard was introduced.
Management says October retail vehicle sales fell about 32% YoY to about 20 lakh units because festive timing shifted last year's sales into October; MCSL disbursements still rose sharply.
Two-wheeler yield on MCSL's own book is 21.5-22%; the blended yield rose as lower-yielding co-lending shrank.
Industry vehicle finance grew 21% in H1 FY27; two-wheeler grew about 16%. MCSL's two-wheeler market share is about 2.5-3%.
Account aggregator use: about 40-45% of two-wheeler loans and about 65% of car and CV loans.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving retail book growth and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed growth to an in-house origination scorecard that lifted approval rates to 70-75%, and targets an exit AUM near Rs 4,200 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did two-wheeler yield rise from 20% to 22%?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower-yielding co-lending shrank by over 50%, so MCSL's own book yield of 21.5-22% now drives the blended yield, which management expects to sustain.

qa_highlights.question: How big will car and CV become?
qa_highlights.answer: Management wants car and CV at more than 50%, or closer to 60%, of the overall book over the next two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the deposit growth and what are the next steps?
qa_highlights.answer: The AA rating and online FD platform allow PAN India deposits at rates above banks and NBFCs, with an average ticket below Rs 5 lakh; the FD book grew about 250% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why is NII not growing in line with the loan book?
qa_highlights.answer: Repayments offset sourcing, and co-lending at a 12-12.5% yield is rolling off; the CFO expects about Rs 200 crore of lower-yielding book to remain by March and NII growth to improve in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ARC recoveries lead to write-backs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recoveries are better than expected, with ARC 1 nearing closure and ARC 2 expected near 80-85% by next year; the Phoenix pool recoveries were about Rs 2-2.5 crore per month over the last 6-7 months.

risks_watch: GNPA rose QoQ to 4.61%, and the dealer channel at 4.56% and group channel at 5.70% GNPA need to fall to bring asset quality to the ~6-7% target the analyst referenced.
Car and CV and used car businesses are cash-burning and loss-making; their breakeven timelines (CV by end FY27, car by Q1 FY28) are key ROA drivers.

Management's own Q2 call notes contain internal inconsistencies, such as the impairment figure of Rs 256 crore quoted and the Rs 15 crore up-money case flagged for checking, so the figures need verification against the filed results.
Rising impairment is possible in the coming quarters if collections weaken.
Bank cost reduction (0.25-0.30% from the rating upgrade) and the effect of the PAN India FD rollout on borrowing costs remain to be seen.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, funding and forward flow, with specific numeric targets; more cautious on profitability, which management tied to the two new businesses breaking even later. Some answers were loose on numbers, which the audience should verify against the filings.
key_quotes: We don't intend to pursue growth at the expense of asset quality.
Our emphasis will always be on a profitable growth supported by stronger underwriting and better risk management.

growth.why: AUM guided to exit FY27 near Rs 4,200 crore from Rs 3,530 crore (about 19% further growth), backed by record October disbursements of Rs 306 crore and Rs 400+ crore per month guided from November, plus a 0.25-0.30% bank cost cut from the AA upgrade; no new capacity is being added and no explicit revenue growth % is guided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Bank borrowing cost to fall a further 0.25-0.30% after the AA rating and about 0.10% more by March 2027, while own-book two-wheeler yield of 21.5-22% replaces lower-yielding co-lending (Rs 382 crore, down 52% YoY from Rs 791 crore), though impairment is guided to rise to about 2% of book by March 2027 and CV/car remain loss-making.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new physical capacity (branches, plants) is discussed; the only build-out is in-house underwriting scorecards/BREs for CV and used car moving by December 2026, plus a PAN India FD campaign that uses the existing digital platform.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: AUM guided to exit FY27 closer to Rs 4,200 crore from Rs 3,530 crore (about 19% further growth), backed by record October disbursements of Rs 306 crore and Rs 400+ crore per month guided from November, with approval rates lifted to 70-75% from 45-50%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed and there is no utilisation figure; the business is asset-light, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says recoveries are better than expected (Phoenix pool at about Rs 2-2.5 crore per month, ARC 1 nearing closure), which could support write-backs, but no formal revenue or margin guidance is raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: GNPA rose QoQ to 4.61% (from 5.76% a year ago, with Q1 flattered by an ARC sale), group channel GNPA is 5.70%, and impairment of Rs 21.44 crore in Q2 alone is running well above the ~2% book level guided for March 2027 pace, so profit guidance could slip if collections weaken.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CV and used car are in an investment phase with the book at Rs 350-356 crore and Rs 215 crore respectively; car and CV are to rise to 50-60% of the book over two years, but no specific new product launch is dated.

rows.label: CV breakeven by end FY27 and car breakeven by Q1 FY28
rows.why: Management guided CV breakeven by end of FY27 and car by Q1 FY28; CV disbursements rose over 100% in H1, but used car is still loss-making with a Rs 215 crore book.

rows.label: Bank borrowing cost cut from AA rating
rows.why: Bank cost expected to fall a further 0.25-0.30% after the AA upgrade and about 0.10% more by March 2027, having already fallen 0.61% on bank loans this quarter.

rows.label: Co-lending run-off completes
rows.why: No new co-lending is being done and the last active partner closed in Q1; the Rs 382 crore book is rolling off at a 12-12.5% yield, with about Rs 200 crore expected to remain by March.

tone.note: Management was confident on AUM growth, funding costs, the AA rating and forward flow, but cautious on profitability, tying it to CV and car breaking even later; analysts pushed on why NII lagged the loan book and on asset quality, and some management figures were loose and need checking against fil
